findings.highlight: UhI don’t want either.
findings.evidenceJa: えいや、どっちもいらないけど
findings.governingReading: Shirou gives a flustered “No—neither,” before redirecting the conversation.
findings.explanation: The displayed English fuses “Uh” and “I,” damaging the opening response.

findings.highlight: What?
findings.evidenceJa: いいけど、なに？
findings.governingReading: Rin agrees that he may ask and asks what it is.
findings.explanation: Bare “What?” removes her permission and makes the reply markedly more abrupt.

findings.highlight: You said something about there being another Master at our school.
findings.evidenceJa: そいつが何かしてるって
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls that the other Master is doing something at school.
findings.explanation: The English omits the unknown Master’s action, reducing his question to mere existence.

findings.highlight: who’s doing things like what we just saw.
findings.evidenceJa: さっきみたいなコトを繰り返してるのよ
findings.governingReading: The Master has been repeatedly doing things like the attack they just witnessed.
findings.explanation: The English omits 繰り返してる, losing that the predation is recurrent.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka said she would’ve died if we hadn’t found her.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂が駆けつけなかったら命を落としていたという。
findings.governingReading: Rin said the girl would have died had Rin not rushed to her.
findings.explanation: The English changes Rin’s sole emergency intervention into Shirou and Rin jointly finding the victim.

findings.highlight: Wha[line3]using the students as sacrifices… Is that Master insane!?
findings.evidenceJa: な[line3]生徒を生け贄にするって、正気かそいつ！？
findings.governingReading: Shirou stammers in horror at sacrificing students.
findings.explanation: The English visibly fuses the broken “Wha” with “using.”

findings.highlight: I was trying to continue my peaceful everyday life.
findings.evidenceJa: 平然と学校という日常に浸っていた
findings.governingReading: Without the needed resolve, Shirou had calmly remained immersed in the everyday world represented by school.
findings.explanation: The English adds an intentional attempt and “peaceful,” while omitting the self-accusing 平然 and the school-as-daily-life image.

findings.highlight: No, you’re wrong.
findings.evidenceJa: いや、そうじゃないんだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Rin’s anxious interpretation is not what he means.
findings.explanation: “You’re wrong” turns a correction of the misunderstanding into a direct accusation against Rin.

findings.highlight: I just thought that I’d never be able to beat you.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえには勝てないなって、そう思った
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he feels he cannot measure up to Rin in resolve.
findings.explanation: “Never” adds permanent inability and “beat” invites a literal combat reading contrary to the scene’s admiration.

findings.highlight: so I try to tell her how I feel.
findings.evidenceJa: せめてこんな台詞で、精一杯の気持ちを口にした。
findings.governingReading: Unable to apologize, Shirou at least puts as much feeling as he can into these particular words.
findings.explanation: The English omits せめて, こんな台詞, and 精一杯, flattening the constrained emotional effort.

findings.highlight: This isn’t about that previous fight
findings.evidenceJa: 別にさっきのコトじゃなくてだな
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists his praise is not simply about what happened earlier.
findings.explanation: The English specifies a fight where さっきのコト leaves the recent matter implicit, prematurely fixing the referent.

findings.highlight: She attacks me with a smile that makes my heart jump.
findings.evidenceJa: ドキッとするぐらい軽やかな笑顔で、とんでもない奇襲をされた。
findings.governingReading: Rin’s startlingly light smile delivers an outrageous surprise attack: her truce proposal.
findings.explanation: The English omits the smile’s lightness and とんでもない, and makes the metaphor sound like a direct attack rather than an unexpected proposal.

findings.highlight: I personally want to take care of this other Master before you.
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方より先にあっちを片づけておきたいの。
findings.governingReading: Rin wants to dispose of the other Master before dealing with Shirou.
findings.explanation: English “before you” can mean before Shirou acts, obscuring that Shirou is the later opponent in Rin’s priority order.

findings.highlight: So do you want to cooperate and look for this other Master?
findings.evidenceJa: だからそれまで休戦して、二人でさっきのマスターを捜さない？
findings.governingReading: Rin proposes a truce lasting until that enemy is handled, during which the two will search jointly.
findings.explanation: The English omits both the explicit truce and its endpoint, presenting only cooperation.

findings.highlight: stop Masters that will hurt innocent people.
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係な人間を巻き込むマスターを止める為に戦う
findings.governingReading: Shirou chose to fight in order to stop a Master who embroils uninvolved people.
findings.explanation: The English changes involvement into direct harm, 無関係 into moral innocence, and the relevant Master into a generalized plural class.

findings.highlight: We’re just promising that we won’t attack each other.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ休戦協定を結んだだけよ
findings.governingReading: Rin insists they have only concluded a formal truce agreement.
findings.explanation: The English weakens a concluded pact into an informal promise and substitutes its presumed behavior for the stated agreement.

findings.highlight: She declares so.
findings.evidenceJa: 断言する声。
findings.governingReading: Her voice states the promise decisively and without qualification.
findings.explanation: Generic narration loses the force carried specifically by Rin’s voice and 断言.

findings.highlight: Please give me your best regards, Tohsaka.
findings.evidenceJa: これからよろしくな、遠坂
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks Rin to work well with him from here on.
findings.explanation: The stock literal “give me your best regards” is non-idiomatic and obscures the forward-looking partnership gesture.

findings.highlight: so at least be of some use to me, okay?
findings.evidenceJa: せいぜい役に立ってよね
findings.governingReading: Rin barbedly tells Shirou to make himself as useful as he possibly can.
findings.explanation: “At least” reverses せいぜい from a maximizer into a minimizer and weakens her demanding tease.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka sounds ungracious.
findings.evidenceJa: 憎まれ口を叩く遠坂。
findings.governingReading: Rin makes a deliberately barbed, contrary remark.
findings.explanation: “Ungracous” gives a vague social judgment and loses the performed verbal hostility that Shirou reads through.

findings.highlight: she firmly shakes my hand.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の手は、しっかり俺の手を握り返してきた
findings.governingReading: Rin firmly grips Shirou’s hand back in response.
findings.explanation: A generic handshake removes 握り返す, the reciprocity that proves sincerity beneath her words.

findings.highlight: We talk about unimportant stuff for a while.
findings.evidenceJa: とりとめのない会話が続く。
findings.governingReading: Their desultory, loosely connected conversation continues.
findings.explanation: The English judges the content unimportant instead of describing its rambling structure.

findings.highlight: As Tohsaka Rin is the head of the Tohsaka family, she is the supervisor of this land even though she’s young.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の家を任されている遠坂凛は、この若さにしてここ一帯の管理人なのだそうだ。
findings.governingReading: Rin, entrusted with the Tohsaka house, is already manager of the surrounding territory at her young age.
findings.explanation: The English invents explicit family-head status and makes it the cause, replacing the source’s entrusted responsibility.

findings.highlight: they didn’t know about his son, who is a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: その息子である俺という魔術師の存在を知り得なかった
findings.governingReading: The Tohsaka family had no means of knowing that Kiritsugu’s son Shirou existed as a magus.
findings.explanation: Simple nonknowledge loses 知り得なかった, the epistemic impossibility created by Kiritsugu’s concealment.

findings.highlight: I only know a bit of other things.
findings.evidenceJa: 他の魔術は名称とか概要とか、そんな事しか判らない。
findings.governingReading: Of other magecraft, Shirou knows only names and broad outlines.
findings.explanation: The English removes both concrete limits and even the explicit referent of other magecraft.

findings.highlight: that was the best magic I’ve ever done.
findings.evidenceJa: 今までで一番上手く出来た魔術だった
findings.governingReading: That reinforcement was the most successfully executed magecraft Shirou had ever managed.
findings.explanation: “Best magic I’ve ever done” is unnatural and can suggest the spell itself was best rather than his execution.

findings.highlight: is that something to be angry about?
findings.evidenceJa: 今のつっこむところか？
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether that was really the point for Rin to call out or retort to.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the comic conversational role of つっこむ with anger.

findings.highlight: We should be hiding the scope of our power
findings.evidenceJa: 手の内は隠しておくべきだし
findings.governingReading: Magi should keep their hand, capabilities, and methods concealed.
findings.explanation: “Scope of our power” narrows tactical information and techniques to power magnitude.

findings.highlight: magic is not something to hide desperately.
findings.evidenceJa: 相手がなんであれ、魔術は必死になって隠す事じゃない
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu taught that magecraft is not something to conceal desperately regardless of who the other person is.
findings.explanation: The English omits 相手がなんであれ, an important universal limit on Kiritsugu’s secrecy rule.

findings.highlight: He always told me that I shouldn’t learn magic and that I could quit any time I wanted.
findings.evidenceJa: 止めたければいつでも止めろって口癖だったぞ
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu habitually told Shirou that if he wanted to stop, he should stop at any time.
findings.explanation: The English changes an imperative granting active permission to stop into a statement of abstract ability.

findings.highlight: If you’re taught by such a character, I can’t approve of you as a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなヤツに鍛えられた貴方も、魔術師なんて認めないから
findings.governingReading: Rin refuses to recognize Shirou as a magus because he was trained by such a man.
findings.explanation: The English makes completed training conditional/present and weakens her volitional refusal to recognize him into inability to approve.

findings.highlight: Then, Tohsaka’s enmity disappears as if she’s regained her composure.
findings.evidenceJa: 我に返ったかのように敵意を消した。
findings.governingReading: Rin extinguishes her hostility as though suddenly returning to herself.
findings.explanation: “Regained her composure” replaces a break-and-return in self-awareness with ordinary emotional control.

findings.highlight: It was my fault.
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと、どうかしてた。
findings.governingReading: Rin apologizes that she was briefly not herself or acting strangely.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her account of altered behavior with a generic admission of blame.

findings.highlight: after a few years of study
findings.evidenceJa: 何年も魔術を鍛えていて
findings.governingReading: After training his magecraft for years and years.
findings.explanation: “A few years” narrows the emphatic 何年も and “study” weakens sustained practical training.

findings.highlight: do I feel a chill?
findings.evidenceJa: もの凄く背筋が寒い
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels an extraordinary chill run down his spine.
findings.explanation: The English drops the body image and extreme intensity.

findings.highlight: a single magus
findings.evidenceJa: 独り身の魔術師
findings.governingReading: A solitary, unaffiliated magus without a lineage or organization.
findings.explanation: “Single magus” is ambiguous with unmarried status and obscures the institutional isolation Rin is explaining.

findings.highlight: your dad never did anything against that.
findings.evidenceJa: そのあたりの努力をまったくしなかった貴方の父親
findings.governingReading: Rin condemns Kiritsugu for making no effort at all toward succession safeguards.
findings.explanation: “Never did anything against that” suggests opposition rather than failure to undertake the required effort.

findings.highlight: ‘Magic’ of a magus isn’t just his magic.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師の『魔術』は、その魔術師だけのものじゃない。
findings.governingReading: A magus’s magecraft does not belong only to that individual magus.
findings.explanation: The repeated “magic” obscures the work’s 魔術 category and produces awkward English at a central inheritance explanation.

findings.highlight: The responsibility isn’t just yours.
findings.evidenceJa: その責任は、もう自分だけの物じゃなくなるのよ
findings.governingReading: Once magecraft is inherited, its responsibility no longer belongs only to oneself.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the generic inheritor’s responsibility directly to Shirou, who lacks the Crest and is the counterexample under discussion.

findings.highlight: a successor and an inheritor.
findings.evidenceJa: 後継者であり伝承者でもある
findings.governingReading: The child is both successor and transmitter or bearer of the tradition.
findings.explanation: “Inheritor” repeats receipt and loses 伝承者’s duty to carry and transmit the lineage onward.

findings.highlight: the duty of the ‘magus’
findings.evidenceJa: “魔術師”という家系の義務
findings.governingReading: The transformation of a human child is the duty of the lineage or house called “magus.”
findings.explanation: The English assigns the duty to an individual magus and omits the family-line institution Rin is defining.

findings.highlight: How much she sacrificed to train
findings.evidenceJa: どれだけ修練を積み重ね、どれだけ自分を犠牲にしてきたか
findings.governingReading: How much training Rin accumulated and how much of herself she separately sacrificed.
findings.explanation: The English collapses two parallel measures into sacrifice undertaken merely in order to train.

findings.highlight: I can’t put myself in her place, no matter how hard I try.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が、遠坂になれる訳ではない
findings.governingReading: Even if Shirou imagines her experience, he cannot become Rin herself.
findings.explanation: The English changes an irreducible identity boundary into difficulty empathizing and invents strenuous effort.

findings.highlight: why you considered me your enemy?
findings.evidenceJa: 俺を目の仇にしてたのか？
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether Rin had singled him out as a hated target.
findings.explanation: Generic enemy status loses the obsessive, targeted hostility in 目の仇.

findings.highlight: I can’t approve of you.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師としては認められないもの。
findings.governingReading: Rin cannot recognize Shirou specifically as a magus.
findings.explanation: The English omits the domain and sounds like rejection of Shirou as a person, despite her explicit statement that she does not dislike him.

findings.highlight: That’s why I had to teach you a lesson!
findings.evidenceJa: つい灸を据えるっていうか、つっつきたくなったのっ！
findings.governingReading: Rin says she impulsively wanted to teach him a lesson—or rather, to poke and provoke him.
findings.explanation: The English adds necessity, removes つい, and deletes her self-correction into a more playful provoking impulse.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka ponders for a bit.
findings.evidenceJa: むー、とばつが悪そうに唸ったあと
findings.governingReading: Rin groans “mm” in visible embarrassment or awkwardness.
findings.explanation: The English replaces vocal embarrassment with silent thought.

findings.highlight: She complains about something strange.
findings.evidenceJa: よく分からない文句を口にした。
findings.governingReading: Rin voices a complaint Shirou does not quite understand.
findings.explanation: The English moves the evaluation from Shirou’s lack of understanding to the complaint being objectively strange.

findings.highlight: I realize I’ve been forgetting about it all along.
findings.evidenceJa: 完全に失念していた。
findings.governingReading: Shirou realizes the fact had completely slipped his mind.
findings.explanation: The English turns a completed lapse into continuous forgetting “all along.”

findings.highlight: The man that almost got his head cut off by Saber that night.
findings.evidenceJa: あの夜、セイバーと打ち合い、その首を斬り落とされかけたサーヴァント。
findings.governingReading: The Servant who traded blows with Saber that night and nearly had his head cut off.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the near beheading but omits their direct exchange of blows.

findings.highlight: The man that tried to shoot Saber along with Berserker.
findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーと戦うセイバーを無視して、もろともに葬り去ろうとした男。
findings.governingReading: The man who disregarded Saber fighting Berserker and tried to annihilate them both together.
findings.explanation: The English invents shooting as the mechanism and omits Archer’s disregard for Saber’s ongoing fight.

findings.highlight: I hate him.
findings.evidenceJa: こいつは嫌いだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou dislikes Archer.
findings.explanation: “Hate” strengthens 嫌い beyond the source’s stated aversion.

findings.highlight: I probably will never be able to accept him.
findings.evidenceJa: たぶん、どうやっても受け入れる事はできない
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks that probably no possible approach would let him accept Archer.
findings.explanation: The English converts the manner impossibility どうやっても into temporal permanence “never.”

findings.highlight: I appreciate that.
findings.evidenceJa: 願ったり叶ったりだ。
findings.governingReading: Archer’s reciprocal dislike is exactly what Shirou could have wished for.
findings.explanation: “I appreciate that” loses the emphatic idiom of an outcome perfectly suiting his wishes.

findings.highlight: Since he can’t go out there dressed like he is
findings.evidenceJa: あの姿のまま外に出る訳にはいかない
findings.governingReading: Archer cannot go outside while remaining in that manifested form.
findings.explanation: The English treats the problem as his clothing rather than the visibility of a materialized Servant form.

findings.highlight: I recall the female student.
findings.evidenceJa: 倒れていた女生徒の姿が浮かぶ。
findings.governingReading: The image of the female student lying collapsed rises in Shirou’s mind.
findings.explanation: The English removes the visible collapsed state that connects Rin’s explanation to immediate bodily evidence.

findings.highlight: wants to use everyone as sacrifices to make his or her Servant stronger.
findings.evidenceJa: うちの生徒をみんな生け贄にして、自分のサーヴァントを強くしようって魂胆なんでしょ
findings.governingReading: Rin infers that the Master’s scheme is to sacrifice all of their school’s students to strengthen that Master’s Servant.
findings.explanation: “Everyone” broadens the victims beyond students, while flat “wants” removes 魂胆’s pejorative scheme and なんでしょ’s inferential status.

findings.highlight: everyone inside will weaken and die
findings.evidenceJa: みんな衰弱死するでしょうね。
findings.governingReading: Rin forecasts that everyone on the grounds would likely die of debilitation.
findings.explanation: The English makes the forecast categorical and splits the specific causal death 衰弱死 into a generic sequence of weakening and dying.

findings.highlight: Why are you depressed?
findings.evidenceJa: さっきから落ち込んじゃって。
findings.governingReading: Rin asks why Shirou has been downcast since a little earlier.
findings.explanation: The English omits the ongoing duration and uses the stronger, potentially clinical “depressed” for an immediate drop in spirits.

findings.highlight: She looks at me uneasily.
findings.evidenceJa: 不安そうに覗き込んでくる。
findings.governingReading: Rin anxiously leans or peers in toward Shirou’s face.
findings.explanation: Generic looking removes the close physical movement and intimacy of 覗き込んでくる.

findings.highlight: do you want to make peace for now?
findings.evidenceJa: とりあえず休戦しない？
findings.governingReading: Rin proposes a provisional truce.
findings.explanation: “Make peace” suggests broader reconciliation and blurs the technical ceasefire whose narrow duration the scene immediately defines.

findings.highlight: it’ll be great if you can help me.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂が力を貸してくれるなら頼もしい
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Rin lending her power would be reassuring and dependable.
findings.explanation: Generic “great” removes his explicit reliance on Rin’s capability.

findings.highlight: She looks away as she says so.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の目を見ずに語って、遠坂は顔を逸らした。
findings.governingReading: Rin speaks without meeting Shirou’s eyes and then turns her face away.
findings.explanation: The English collapses sustained lack of eye contact and subsequent turning into one simultaneous generic look away.

findings.highlight: What Tohsaka thought when she was raised in this house…
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂がどんな思いでこの家で育ったのか。
findings.governingReading: With what feelings Rin grew up in this house.
findings.explanation: The English reduces an enduring emotional experience during upbringing to a singular cognitive thought and uses passive “was raised.”

findings.highlight: I stare at her for affirmation.
findings.evidenceJa: だろ、と視線で問いかけてみる。
findings.governingReading: Shirou tries asking “right?” with his gaze.
findings.explanation: “Stare at her for affirmation” is unnatural and turns a tentative visual question into a demand for validation.

findings.highlight: It must be the same for Archer
findings.evidenceJa: それはアーチャーも同じなのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether Archer feels the same aversion.
findings.explanation: “Must be” makes the reciprocal judgment categorical where のか leaves it as Shirou’s question or inference.

findings.highlight: Please do your best, Archer.
findings.evidenceJa: よろしくねアーチャー。
findings.governingReading: Rin entrusts Shirou’s escort to Archer with a relational よろしく formula.
findings.explanation: “Do your best” reframes the instruction as performance effort rather than entrusting the person and task to him.

findings.highlight: he was also against the fact that I wanted to be a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師になるのには反対してた
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu opposed Shirou becoming a magus.
findings.explanation: The English makes the object of opposition the fact of Shirou’s desire, obscuring whether Kiritsugu opposed the wish or the resulting identity.

findings.highlight: It seemed like he taught me magic because I wouldn’t give up.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が諦めないから仕方なく教えたって感じだった
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu seemed to teach only reluctantly because Shirou would not give up.
findings.explanation: The English keeps Shirou’s persistence but drops 仕方なく, Kiritsugu’s no-choice reluctance.

findings.highlight: I want to know about your family.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮家の事情が知りたい
findings.governingReading: Rin wants to know the Emiya household’s circumstances and background.
findings.explanation: Generic family information removes 事情 and the investigative focus on why this mage household differs.

findings.highlight: proper lineage
findings.evidenceJa: 由緒正しい家系
findings.governingReading: An established lineage with a distinguished history.
findings.explanation: “Proper lineage” sounds merely genealogically correct and loses the family’s recognized historical standing.

findings.highlight: Actually, he hid the fact that he was a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: というより、魔術師である事自体隠していたらしい。
findings.governingReading: Rather, it appears Kiritsugu concealed even the fact that he was a magus.
findings.explanation: The English changes らしい from reported inference to fact and というより from corrective refinement to “actually.”

findings.highlight: a lone-wolf magus that came from the outside
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮切嗣は、外からやってきた一匹狼の魔術師だった。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu was a lone-wolf magus who came from elsewhere.
findings.explanation: The English uses inanimate “that” for a person and the Japanese-shaped phrase “came from the outside.”

findings.highlight: it’s only recently that she actually became able to protect the land.
findings.evidenceJa: 実質的に土地を守れるようになったのはつい最近だという。
findings.governingReading: Shirou reports that Rin only recently became practically capable of protecting the land.
findings.explanation: The English drops という and states the attributed account as direct narrator fact.

findings.highlight: You don’t have any knowledge other than the magic you can use, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が扱える魔術以外、魔道の知識はないわけね？
findings.governingReading: Rin confirms Shirou lacks knowledge of the magecraft discipline beyond the technique he can use.
findings.explanation: The English is hard to parse and collapses 魔道, broader disciplinary knowledge, into “the magic you can use.”

findings.highlight: I can only use the ‘strengthening’ magic.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が使えるのは“強化”だけだからな。
findings.governingReading: The sole technique Shirou can use is Reinforcement.
findings.explanation: “The strengthening magic” treats the named Fate technique as a generic descriptive phrase and uses the wrong technical register.

findings.highlight: Why are you telling me something like that!?
findings.evidenceJa: なんでそんな事までわたしに喋るのよ、アンタは！
findings.governingReading: Rin demands why Shirou would tell even that much to her, addressing him roughly as アンタ.
findings.explanation: The English loses まで’s excessive extent and omits the exasperated vocative, weakening her pointed outburst.

findings.highlight: Then. She gets mad like it’s her own affair.
findings.evidenceJa: なぜか我がコトのように怒り出す。
findings.governingReading: For some reason, Rin begins getting angry as though it were her own affair.
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou’s なぜか puzzlement and replaces it with a clumsy “Then.” fragment.

findings.highlight: not to be bound by rules.
findings.evidenceJa: あんまり規則に捕らわれるな
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu likely meant not to become too constrained by rules.
findings.explanation: Dropping あんまり turns a warning against excessive rule fixation into categorical rejection of being bound by rules.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka grits her teeth.
findings.evidenceJa: ぎり、という音。
findings.governingReading: Shirou hears a grinding sound without yet explicitly assigning its physical source.
findings.explanation: The English resolves the sensory cue into a definite action by Rin, removing the narration’s momentary observational distance.

findings.highlight: She’s showing enmity like never before.
findings.evidenceJa: 敵意を剥き出しにしている。
findings.governingReading: Rin has her hostility laid completely bare.
findings.explanation: Abstract “showing enmity” weakens the visceral exposed-hostility image in 剥き出し.

findings.highlight: my father was a great magus.
findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣は立派な魔術師だったぞ？
findings.governingReading: Shirou directly challenges Rin that Kiritsugu was an admirable, proper magus.
findings.explanation: The English drops the challenging ぞ？ contour and familiar Kiritsugu reference, making the defense flatter and “great” potentially about power.

findings.highlight: That what?
findings.evidenceJa: その、なんだろう。
findings.governingReading: Shirou internally hesitates over what Rin was about to say.
findings.explanation: “That what?” reads as a direct challenge and loses the self-interrupting narrative hesitation.

findings.highlight: Everyone’s ways are different.
findings.evidenceJa: 鍛え方は人それぞれだものね。
findings.governingReading: Rin concedes that methods of training differ from person to person.
findings.explanation: The English omits the training object and broadens her repair into a vague statement about everyone’s ways.

findings.highlight: it’s not my place to tell you something.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮くんをどうこう言える筈がなかった
findings.governingReading: Rin admits she had no standing to criticize or pass judgment on Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Tell you something” is vague and removes both criticism and the strength of her self-correction.

findings.highlight: Did something annoy you? Um, like the method Father taught me
findings.evidenceJa: なにか気に障った事でもあったのか。その、切嗣の教え方とか
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether something offended Rin, perhaps the way Kiritsugu taught him.
findings.explanation: “Annoy” weakens offense, while “the method Father taught me” is malformed and obscures that he means Kiritsugu’s teaching method.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka asked me that question, and it’s now getting into how I learned magic.
findings.evidenceJa: という遠坂の提案で、俺が魔術をどう習っていたのか、という話になったのだ。
findings.governingReading: At Rin’s suggestion, their conversation turns to how Shirou was taught magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English changes 提案 into a question and uses the malformed “it’s now getting into,” obscuring how the discussion arose.

findings.highlight: What is that? Did your dad really say such a thing?
findings.evidenceJa: なにそれ。衛宮くんの父親、本気でそんなコト言ってたの？
findings.governingReading: Rin reacts colloquially, “What is that supposed to mean?” and asks whether Kiritsugu truly said it.
findings.explanation: “What is that?” sounds like a question about an object and loses the idiomatic challenge to Shirou’s account.
